facts.text: Hollister sprang up in 1909 as the service hub for the Salmon Tract irrigation project, with the Salmon Dam opening 80,000 acres to settlers.
Hollister sits on the east bank of Salmon Falls Creek in Twin Falls County.
The hottest recorded temperature in Hollister was 108°F on July 14, 1922, while the coldest was –29°F on January 8, 1937.
Conflicts between cattle and sheep interests culminated in an 1887 law favoring ranchers, while overgrazing and harsh winters like 1874‑75 depleted forage, prompting shifts toward hay production.
Early settlers on the Oregon Trail crossed Hollister’s arid sagebrush, stopping at water sources like Rock Creek and Salmon Falls Creek.
A 1912 bond election approved a $30,000 brick schoolhouse that symbolized local optimism and served as an educational cornerstone until high school consolidation with Filer in 1948.
